title: introduce-ephemeral-gpu-pools-and-cross-project-iam-sharding
author: Maya Singh
description: Motivation: customers running Private deployments asked for a safer workflow to create short-lived GPU capacity for burst workloads and better isolation of IAM roles across cloud projects/accounts. This PR introduces two cooperating Terraform modules plus a migration plan: (1) tf-module/gpu-ephemeral-pool - supports creation of ephemeral GPU node pools with predictable lifecycle hooks, annotated leases, and a small controller-friendly tag surface to enable external reclaimers; (2) tf-module/iam-shard - supports cross-project/account IAM role sharding and immutable role templates so we can shard service-account bindings by tenant, limiting blast radius and simplifying key rotation. The change also includes a state-indexing helper (scripts/tfstate-indexer) that generates a mapping of legacy resources to new shard keys to allow a non-destructive migration of state between backends. Risk/compatibility: no resource renames are performed in-place; migrations are additive and provide a hands-off dry-run mode. Rollback: the indexer emits reverse mappings and we keep the old state backend intact until the migration is validated. Summary of what changed: new gpu-ephemeral-pool module (variables for pool lifetime, min/max, taints/labels, node affinity selectors), new iam-shard module (role templates, per-tenantTrustBindings, optional external KMS key binding), migration utilities (tfstate-indexer + migration plan docs), example usage for Private installer (examples/private/ephemeral-gpu-playbook.md), updated README and CHANGELOG entry. Testing: unit-level terraform validate/tflint across modules, a staged e2e in our infra-backend where ephemeral pools are created and drained, and a dry-run migration against a snapshot of an existing tfstate. See CI checks summary below. Checklist: - [x] module interface and docs - [x] migration tooling and dry-run - [x] unit/linters passing - [x] e2e smoke on staging - [x] rollout/rollback playbooks added Migration notes: run scripts/tfstate-indexer --input <legacy-state> --output mapping.json --dry-run first; apply iam-shard with mapping.json in the variable; then create ephemeral pools for the tenant and validate workloads before updating production router policies. Related: builds on ideas from ENG-6689 (tenant leases) but focuses on ephemeral capacity and cross-account IAM sharding.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: request_changes: We should avoid creating long-lived service accounts per tenant; can we make the iam-shard generate ephemeral credentials or recommend workload identity where supported?

Maya Singh: reply: Agreed; the module defaults to workload-identity where available and exposes an optional service_account_template only for legacy clouds. Added docs and a flag 'enable_legacy_sa' (default false).
Sofia Patel: comment: The indexer script is python2-compatible; prefer python3 and add tests for mapping edge cases (resources without tags).
Maya Singh: reply: Switched indexer to python3, added unit tests for missing tags and null owners, and clarified the dry-run output format in README.

Noah Reed: approve: Verified tfplan for a staging tenant and performed a drain-recreate cycle against a staging cluster. I ran e2e smoke and saw <1s p10 token latency regression. Good to go with migration guard.
merge_outcome: merged (squash) by Maya Singh after approvals
release_notes: - Added modules: gpu-ephemeral-pool and iam-shard. - Added migration tooling: tfstate-indexer for non-destructive state mapping. - Examples and playbook for creating tenant-scoped ephemeral GPU pools. - No in-place renames; migration is additive and reversible via indexer reverse mapping.
notes_for_ops: Migration steps: 1) snapshot legacy tfstate; 2) run tfstate-indexer --input snapshot.tfstate --output mapping.json --dry-run; 3) review mapping.json and run without --dry-run to produce a namespaced mapping; 4) apply iam-shard with mapping.json; 5) create ephemeral pools per playbook and validate; 6) optionally switch router/placement policies to prefer ephemeral pools. Rollback: re-apply legacy state and destroy newly created ephemeral pools after validation. Support: tag @infra-priv-deploy in Linear if migration issues occur.
security_considerations: IAM sharding reduces blast radius by scoping bindings; module defaults to workload-identity and optional KMS binding is gated behind a flag. Indexer avoids secret outputs and never emits service account keys. Ops must follow the playbook for key rotation and do a staged rollout.
testing_summary: Local terraform validate across module matrix, tflint, python3 unit tests for indexer, staging e2e smoke: ephemeral pool create+drain cycle, migration dry-run applied to a tfstate snapshot; integration required manual approval in CI.
